capitals.name: Bogota
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Bogota. The Congress of Angostura (1819) and the Congress of Cucuta (1821) were held elsewhere.

correction.text: the patriot-held New Granada of Cliopatria's 1820-1821 row, standing for the land held before Venezuela, Panama and Quito were added

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page dates the republic to 17 December 1819 (infobox) but Cliopatria's row begins in 1822. The page does not describe what land was held in 1819-1821; it says only that Bolivar won an 'unexpected victory in New Granada' and that the 1819 Cundinamarca department became the core of New Granada. Cliopatria's New Granada 1820 shape (Colombia, 1.34 M km2) is used as the bridge, confidence 1.

correction.text: New Granada, Venezuela and Panama, as the republic stood at the end of 1821

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Venezuela ('all of Venezuela except Puerto Cabello was liberated at the Battle of Carabobo', undated on the page) and Panama ('joined the federation in November 1821') are inside by the end of 1821; Quito, Guayaquil and Pasto join 'in 1822'.

2.85 M km2 against the infobox 3.06 M km2 (undated; ratio 0.93). Panama, Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador whole, plus Peruvian Amazon land (Loreto 0.53, Amazonas 0.40, Cajamarca 0.26, Tumbes 0.19) and a little Brazilian Amazonas, which matches the page: the claim 'included parts of northern Peru and northwestern Brazil' and most of the Essequibo. The Peruvian part is a claim that Peru held; see the 1829 Armistice of Piura event.

keyframe_review.note: 4.32 M km2 against the infobox 3.06 M km2 (ratio 1.41). The shape is the 1822 shape plus all of Bolivia (nine departments), 59 percent of Paraguay and a slice of northern Chile: the same land as Cliopatria's Spanish Empire shape for 1822-23. The page never counts Bolivia, Upper Peru or Paraguay in Gran Colombia (it only says Bolivar wrote a constitution 'for Bolivia'), so the extra land is removed and the 1822 shape stands for 1824-1828; in 1829 the Peruvian part leaves (new keyframe 1829). correction.text: the central departments (Boyaca, Cauca, Cundinamarca, Magdalena, Isthmus) that became the State of New Granada

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the whole 1822 extent (2.85 M km2, Venezuela and Ecuador included) to 1833, but Venezuela and Ecuador left in 1830 and Gran Colombia was abolished in November 1831, when the State of New Granada replaced it (20 October 1831 convention; Republic of New Granada by the 1832 constitution). The correct shape for 1830-1831 is the central departments, Colombia and Panama (Panama separated 26 September 1830 and was back by August 1831); from 1832 those cells belong to republic-of-new-granada, whose Cliopatria row only starts in 1834, so 1832-1833 is a gap for that dossier to cover.

region.text: the patriot-held New Granada: Bolivar's 'unexpected victory in New Granada'; the Cundinamarca department 'became the core'

ledger.note: 1819: Gran Colombia is proclaimed at Angostura. Infobox 'Established: December 17, 1819'; the body says the republic 'did not come into being until the Congress of Cucuta (1821) promulgated the Constitution of Cucuta' (30 August 1821, twelve departments). The page does not describe the land held in 1819; the New Granada core is Cliopatria's bridge.

region.text: all of Venezuela except Puerto Cabello

ledger.note: 1821: Venezuela is freed. 'All of Venezuela except Puerto Cabello was liberated at the Battle of Carabobo.' The page gives no date for Carabobo; the Spanish Empire dossier (Spanish American wars of independence page) dates it 24 June 1821.

region.text: Panama, which 'voluntarily became part of it in 1821'

ledger.note: 1821: Panama joins. 'Panama joined the federation in November 1821.'

region.text: Quito and Guayaquil (Pasto, in southern Colombia, is already inside the New Granada shape)

ledger.note: 1822: Quito, Guayaquil and Pasto join. The page lists 'the provinces of Pasto, Guayaquil, and Quito in 1822' without a month; the Spanish Empire dossier dates Pichincha and the fall of Quito to 24 May 1822. Guayaquil was an independent province, not Spanish.

region.text: the Peruvian provinces of Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas in the 1822 shape

ledger.note: 1822: the Peruvian provinces of the claim appear in Cliopatria's shape. The page says the republic claimed 'Jaen and Maynas' and included 'parts of northern Peru'; it does not say when Gran Colombia held them, so the year is the Cliopatria shape's.

region.text: Guayaquil, held by the Peruvian navy and army until 21 July 1829

ledger.note: 1829: Peru holds Guayaquil. 'The city finally surrendered on 19 January 1829' to the Peruvian forces; the Peruvian navy had attacked its defences on 22-24 November 1828 (Gran Colombia-Peru War page).

region.text: Loja (taken at Saraguro, 13 February 1829) and the Cuenca highlands (Portete de Tarqui, 26-27 February 1829)

ledger.note: 1829: Peru invades the south. 'Seized the city of Loja by winning the Battle of Saraguro on the 13 February 1829'; the Portete de Tarqui fight of 26-27 February 'was not decisive'.

region.text: Loja (taken at Saraguro, 13 February 1829) and the Cuenca highlands (Portete de Tarqui, 26-27 February 1829)

ledger.note: 1829: the fighting stops. 'On the 28 February 1829, La Mar and Sucre signed a conditioning document' after Tarqui; the Peruvian invasion 'lost momentum'.

region.text: Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas, recognised as Peruvian territories by the Armistice of Piura

ledger.note: 1829: the Peruvian provinces are conceded. 'On 10 July 1829, the Armistice of Piura recognised the annexation of Guayaquil to Gran Colombia'; Gran Colombia 'recognized Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas as Peruvian territories'. The Larrea-Gual Treaty of 22 September 1829 (in force 27 October on the main page) then affirmed uti possidetis and left the border to a commission.

region.text: Guayaquil, held by the Peruvian navy and army until 21 July 1829

ledger.note: 1829: Peru leaves Guayaquil. It 'remained under Peruvian occupation until 21 July 1829'.

1830: Venezuela leaves. 'On 6 May 1830 the constituent congress was installed in Valencia', confirmed Paez as president and 'declared Venezuela's total autonomy'; on 22 September 1830 the separation 'was definitively consummated'. Paez had mutinied on 30 April 1826.

region.text: the departments of Ecuador, Guayaquil and Azuay

ledger.note: 1830: the Southern District leaves. On 13 May 1830 'the Southern District declared independence, forming the State of Ecuador' (Flores Supreme Head); Guayaquil and Azuay separated on 19-20 May; the constitution of 22 September 1830 united the departments of Azuay, Guayaquil and Ecuador. Pasto and Cauca asked to join Ecuador but the page does not confirm it.
1830: Panama breaks away. 'On 26 September 1830 the Department of the Isthmus separated from Gran Colombia' under Jose Domingo Espinar; a second separation by Juan Eligio Alzuru began on 9 July 1831.
1831: Panama is back. On 29 August 1831 General Tomas de Herrera shot Alzuru and took control of the isthmus; 'after the dictatorship fell in late August 1831, Panama joined the central convention'.

region.text: the central departments (Boyaca, Cauca, Cundinamarca, Magdalena, Isthmus) that became the State of New Granada

ledger.note: 1831: Gran Colombia is abolished. The convention created the State of New Granada on 20 October 1831; 'Gran Colombia was legally abolished' on 21 November 1831 (infobox: 19 November 1831; the main page: the federation 'dissolved in the closing months of 1830 and was formally abolished in 1831'). Bolivar had resigned on 4 May and died on 17 December 1830.

wars.name: Gran Colombia-Peru War

zones.text: Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas, recognised as Peruvian territories by the Armistice of Piura
Guayaquil, held by the Peruvian navy and army until 21 July 1829
Loja (taken at Saraguro, 13 February 1829) and the Cuenca highlands (Portete de Tarqui, 26-27 February 1829)

wars.outcome: Stalemate after Tarqui; the Armistice of Piura (10 July 1829) recognised Guayaquil as Gran Colombian and Tumbes, Jaen and Maynas as Peruvian; the Larrea-Gual Treaty (22 September 1829) ended the war with 'status quo ante bellum' and a boundary commission.
wars.note: Infobox '20 May 1828 - 22 September 1829'; the declaration of war is dated 3 June and 3 July 1828 in two places. Main page: 'On 3 June 1828, Bolivar declared war on Peru over Gran Colombian claims on the Peruvian territories of Jaen and Maynas'.

wars.name: Paez's revolt in Venezuela
wars.outcome: Paez mutinied on 30 April 1826, was amnestied, and led Venezuela out of the union in 1829-1830 (Valencia congress, 6 May and 22 September 1830).
wars.note: No fighting zone is recorded: Venezuela's separation is the ledger's 1830 loss.

certainty.note: The republic's claim rested on uti possidetis and colonial boundaries the Peru war page calls imprecise; the Peruvian, Brazilian and Essequibo frontiers were never fixed (the 1829 treaty left the Peruvian line to a commission). The Venezuelan and Colombian internal departments are administrative, not survey lines.

notes: Cliopatria rows: (1) the 1824-1829 shape (4.32 M km2) includes Bolivia, 59 percent of Paraguay and part of Chile and is corrected to the 1822 shape (no page puts those lands in Gran Colombia); (2) the 1830-1833 shape keeps Venezuela and Ecuador after their 1830 secession and runs two years past the abolition (November 1831): the dossier ends in 1831, and the State/Republic of New Granada must cover 1832-1833 (its Cliopatria row starts 1834) - for the new-granada group, keyframe 'republic-of-new-granada' needs a new 1832-1833 entry. (3) The main page does not date Carabobo, Pichincha or Guayaquil's annexation; those events are confidence 1-2 and the Spanish Empire dossier carries the dates from its own page. (4) Panama in 1821 is a Spanish Empire loss that the Spanish Empire dossier does not list; counterpart spanish-empire used here. (5) Page conflicts: infobox says federal, text says unitary centralist; dissolution 19 November (infobox) vs 21 November 1831; the war declaration on 3 June vs 3 July 1828; Mosquito Shore in the claim (body) vs excluded (infobox). (6) Heads of state are not listed as rulers: the infobox mixes presidents and vice-presidents with overlapping years (Bolivar 1819-1830; Santander 1821-1827; Caycedo, Mosquera and Urdaneta 1830-1831). (7) Essequibo claim ('most of Esequiba') and 'parts of northwestern Brazil' are claims inside the Cliopatria shape, not dated events. (8) Counterparts needing dossiers: none beyond existing rows; 'Republic of Guayaquil'/Free Province of Guayaquil is not a Cliopatria row (Guayaquil Junta 1812-1813 only).
